dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agency heads, appointed regional educators, parents, and secondary school communities through study and reporting.
dimensions.evidence: There is established a multiagency Middle School Mental Health Task Force... to study and survey the resources that are available to parents and educators

dimensions.assessment: Administrative and investigative effects are minor, as members serve without pay and the task force has no subpoena power or additional personnel.
dimensions.evidence: Each member of the Task Force shall serve on the Task Force without pay... The Task Force shall not be entitled to appoint additional personnel.

dimensions.assessment: Minimal fiscal impact, limited to procuring temporary expert services and contingent contract authority subject to appropriations.
dimensions.evidence: To the extent or in the amounts provided in advance in appropriation Acts, the Task Force may contract with and compensate government and private agencies

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a temporary advisory and reporting task force composed of 12 members meeting twice a year.
dimensions.evidence: submit to the Committee on Education and Workforce... and the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions... an annual report

dimensions.assessment: Members serve two-year terms on the task force, conducting studies and submitting annual reports.
dimensions.evidence: Each member of the Task Force shall serve on the Task Force for 2 calendar years.

missing_information: Exact operating budget for the task force is not specified.
importance_detail.rationale: Establishes a non-compensated multiagency task force at the Departments of Education and Health and Human Services to study and report on middle school mental health resources without adding personnel or subpoena power.
